name: Structured output from LLMs
needs: the AI returns broken JSON sometimes
get data my code can use from the model, not prose
extract fields from a document with AI
summary: Getting the model to return data in a fixed shape your code can rely on. Use the provider's schema feature where it exists, then validate the result anyway and decide what happens when it doesn't fit: retry once, fall back, or show an error.
need_when: Your code reads fields out of the model's answer: labels, extracted data, decisions or tool arguments.
skip_when: The output is only text shown to a person.

ways.title: Provider schema enforcement
ways.how: OpenAI Structured Outputs with a strict JSON schema, or tool definitions with an input schema (OpenAI function calling, Anthropic tool use), using strict mode where the provider offers it.
ways.tradeoff: The provider holds the shape in strict mode. Supported schema features are limited, and the model can still refuse or pick wrong values.

ways.title: JSON mode plus your own validation
ways.how: Ask for JSON, parse it, and validate with Pydantic or Zod. JSON mode only promises valid JSON, not your schema.
ways.tradeoff: Works across more models. You handle mismatches yourself.

ways.title: A library
ways.how: Instructor (Python) or the Vercel AI SDK's object generation take a Pydantic or Zod schema and handle retries.
ways.tradeoff: Less glue code. One more dependency to keep current.

prompt:
Make [AI feature] return structured data.

Requirements:
- Define the output schema in [Pydantic/Zod]: field types, required fields, enums for fixed choices, max lengths.
- Use the provider's structured output or tool schema feature with that schema where supported.
- Validate every response against the schema in our code, even when the provider enforces it. Check enum values against our allowed list.
- On invalid output or a refusal, retry once, then fall back to [safe default / non-AI path] and log the failure.
- Never pass model output straight into SQL, shell commands, file paths or HTML.
- Add tests with real sample inputs, plus a mocked malformed response.

Acceptance checks (run each and show me the result):
1. 100 sample inputs all produce output that passes validation, or are handled by the fallback.
2. A mocked response with an unknown enum value is rejected.
3. A mocked malformed response triggers one retry and then the fallback.
4. The schema in the code and the one sent to the provider come from one definition.
acceptance_checks: 100 sample inputs all produce output that passes validation, or are handled by the fallback.
A mocked response with an unknown enum value is rejected.
A mocked malformed response triggers one retry and then the fallback.
The schema in the code and the one sent to the provider come from one definition.
if_you_skip_it: Features that crash on the one response in fifty that isn't valid JSON, or code that acts on made-up field values.
how_derek_runs_it: Custody Journal's tone classifier asks the model for a JSON object, then checks that the label is one of three allowed values and keeps only hits in known categories. Anything that doesn't fit falls back to the keyword classifier.
